artifacts.summary: Resolves the hook's Edit-path scope, the advisory-tier write-time posture, and identifies a settings.json wiring gap (root-files/settings.json alone never propagates to an already-deployed repo; merge-sources/settings-hooks.json must also be edited).

memory_candidates.content: In this repo's extension system, agent-system/extensions/core/root-files/settings.json is install-once only (copied when no project .claude/ copy exists yet) and never propagates to an already-deployed repo on resync. The actual propagation path for new hook registrations into a live .claude/settings.json is agent-system/extensions/core/merge-sources/settings-hooks.json, via manifest.json's merge_targets.settings entry (source: merge-sources/settings-hooks.json, target: .claude/settings.json). A new PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook registration must be added to BOTH files to be both fresh-install-correct and already-deployed-repo-correct; editing only root-files/settings.json silently fails to reach any repo that already has a .claude/ tree.

When building a write-time PreToolUse guard hook that consumes a shared pattern library also used by a repo-wide lint, scope the hook's Edit-path handling to whatever the library's exemption-stripper actually supports: a flat (non-nesting) version-ok toggle (record-version-patterns.sh) only needs a payload-only scan of new_string, not the full disk-reconstruction/occurrence-counting/depth-counting machinery a different sibling hook (validate-no-task-references.sh) built for a depth-counting marker parser (task-reference-patterns.sh). Matching a sibling hook's structure should stop at the point where the underlying library's own semantics diverge.
